items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He came up with that smooth thing which Jo Jones and them did with Basie.

ctx.x: I’m with Lucky Millinder for three years. We played everything between Duke and Cab. What they didn’t want, they shove in Lucky Millinder. Irving Mills was handling Lucky Millinder for a while. Lucky Millinder mess up with the money. Drank it. Throwed it away in the salary. They got mad with him. Said, “We got to get rid of this monkey.” So he never was a success no more, because you couldn’t trust him to bring the salary back in. That was the end of . . . So I’m with Lucky Millinder’s band. Lucky

Millinder’s hitting from here. Going, playing one-nighters here. Going to play a theater there and three or four one-nighters. He’s hitting and missing. He’s walking around all begging poor, but he done lost favor with the big dogs, the people who controlled everything. They said he’s . . . you can’t depend on him. I guess Lucky didn’t like it, people taking a big slice of his money. Some people just can’t stand that, but that’s a part of the game. Them people got to keep their offices going. items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: He stayed in Omaha with me for 3 days in my home

ctx.x: Dannie Barker, the guitar with us player?

That's right and he left the band then. He stayed in Omaha with me for 3 days in my home and I got him a lot of literature and I introduced him to several of the old pioneers and I sent him down to Scott Joplin's home. There was a trumpet player that had lived round in that area that died. He had cancer of the lip, because. I remember seeing him coming out of P. G. Lowry and Abe Wright days. These are great guys that played on the circus. Dannie had a lot of literature. That's the reason he knows what he's…
